panels.title: Command latency per second
Total Time Spent by Command / sec

panels.description: Hit rate shows the percentage of key space lookups that hit a key.
panels.title: Hit ratio per instance

panels.description: Hit rate shows the percentage of key space lookups that hit a key for the cluster.
panels.title: Hit ratio for the cluster

panels.description: Only masters report connected replicas.
panels.title: Connected slaves by instance

panels.description: Per-replica lag in bytes, computed on the master as master_repl_offset - connected_slave_offset_bytes. Only online replicas are shown.
panels.title: Replication Lag (bytes)

panels.description: Per-replica lag in seconds reported by the master (INFO replication "lag" field). Only masters export this.
panels.title: Replication Lag (seconds)

panels.description: 1 = replica link is up, 0 = link is down. Only replicas export this metric.
panels.title: Replication link status

panels.description: Seconds since the replica last interacted with its master. Only replicas export this; it grows when the link is down.
panels.title: Time since last master IO

panels.description: 1 = OK, 0 = error. RDB last bgsave / AOF last write / AOF last background rewrite.
panels.title: Persistence status

panels.description: Seconds since the last successful RDB save. Growing values together with unsaved changes indicate a failing snapshot.
panels.title: RDB last save age

panels.description: Number of write operations since the last successful RDB save.
panels.title: RDB unsaved changes

panels.description: Duration of the last fork. Spikes explain latency and memory spikes during BGSAVE/AOF rewrite.
panels.title: Fork latency

panels.description: Copy-on-write memory used by the last RDB save. Large values explain temporary memory growth.
panels.title: RDB COW size

panels.description: Current AOF size, AOF buffer, and AOF rewrite buffer. Buffer growth can indicate slow disk or rewrite backpressure.
panels.title: AOF size and buffer

panels.description: Pending and delayed fsync operations. Sustained growth indicates slow or stuck disk I/O.
panels.title: AOF fsync backlog

panels.description: 1 = operation in progress. Shows RDB BGSAVE, AOF rewrite, and scheduled AOF rewrite.
panels.title: Persistence in progress

panels.description: Rate of rejected connections and newly accepted connections. Rejected connections usually mean maxclients is exhausted.
panels.title: Rejected connections / churn

panels.description: Largest recent input/output buffers across clients. Large values point to big commands, slow consumers, or stuck connections.
panels.title: Client buffer pressure

panels.description: Rate of error replies, unexpected errors, and errors by type.
panels.title: Error replies

panels.description: Failed and rejected calls per command. Use this to identify the command responsible for application errors.
panels.title: Command failures

panels.description: Number of entries in the slow query log.
panels.title: Slowlog entries

panels.description: Keys removed by expiration and eviction. Compare with key count growth to see whether TTLs are effective.
panels.title: Expired / evicted keys rate

panels.description: Percentage of keys that are already logically expired but still occupy memory.
panels.title: Expired stale percentage

panels.description: Rate at which the expiration cycle hits its time cap. A growing value indicates an expiration backlog.
panels.title: Expire time cap reached

panels.description: Average TTL of keys with an expiration. Near-zero values often indicate missing or misconfigured TTLs.
panels.title: Average TTL

panels.description: Dataset, overhead, and peak memory. Dataset growth means more data; overhead growth points to clients, buffers, or metadata.
panels.title: Memory composition

panels.description: Memory used by normal clients, replica clients, and memory excluded from eviction.
panels.title: Buffer breakdown

panels.description: Absolute fragmentation and allocator RSS overhead. More reliable than the fragmentation ratio for small instances.
panels.title: Fragmentation bytes

panels.description: Change in full and partial resync counts. Repeated full resyncs usually mean the replication backlog is too small or the link is unstable.
panels.title: Full / partial resyncs

panels.description: Replication backlog history divided by configured backlog size. Values near 1 mean partial resync is likely to fail.
panels.title: Replication backlog usage

panels.description: 1 = a replica is receiving a full sync from its master. Lag metrics are not meaningful during a full sync.
panels.title: Full sync in progress

panels.description: 1 = Redis exporter can reach the instance, 0 = it cannot.
panels.title: Instance up

panels.description: 1 = the last scrape failed, 0 = it succeeded. Check this before trusting other panels.
panels.title: Scrape error

panels.description: 1 = uptime decreased during the last 5 minutes, which indicates a restart.
panels.title: Restart detected

panels.description: Sentinel master status and CKQUORUM result. 1 = OK, 0 = fail.
panels.title: Sentinel master status

panels.description: Known and healthy Sentinel/replica counts per monitored master. If ok_sentinels is lower than the quorum, failover cannot proceed.
panels.title: Sentinel quorum

panels.description: 1 = Sentinel is in TILT mode and may make unreliable decisions.
panels.title: Sentinel tilt

panels.description: 1 = cluster state ok, 0 = cluster state fail.
panels.title: Cluster state

panels.description: Assigned, ok, pfail, and fail slot counts.
panels.title: Cluster slots

panels.description: Number of nodes known to the cluster.
panels.title: Cluster known nodes
